gen-butcherman-mulish: Butcherman is dark and raw, its letters never touching and its apertures cut like narrow slots. Mulish does what it does best the other way round: one constant stroke width and wide, horseshoe-open curves that welcome the eye.
gen-butcherman-poppins: Raw and dark, Butcherman keeps every letter well apart from its neighbors. Poppins takes over below with loose, rounded curves and sturdy, tall-bodied lowercase, so paragraphs flow without any thick-thin flicker snagging the eye.
gen-butcherman-roboto-slab: Dark and raw, Butcherman holds its letters apart and squeezes its apertures into slots. Roboto Slab, a slab-serif with open throats, gives paragraphs a precise, structured texture driven by its dominant middle zone.
gen-dafont-abberancy-poppins: Rebellious Abberancy pinches the gap in its c nearly closed and lets capitals barely rise above their neighbors. Poppins smooths things over with clean, modern strokes of uniform weight.
gen-dafont-arkhip-gf-cascadia-mono: Cascadia Mono reads like pins standing in a wide board, its capitals blending into a compact lowercase skyline. But Arkhip, with letters floating apart, sets the pair's sharpest edge: a moderate lowercase height set against a high one.
gen-dafont-arkhip-gf-julius-sans-one: Arkhip floats its geometric letters well apart, with a c open like a bent paperclip. Julius Sans One echoes that spaciousness with wide gaps and open-ended curves, so the two feel like quiet, friendly neighbors.
gen-dafont-arkhip-gf-lexend-exa: Lexend Exa keeps its thickness constant in every direction, with generous curves that stay distinct beside stubby ascenders. And paragraphs of it move smoothly, since Arkhip's floating letters and this body both keep lines crisp and uncrowded.
gen-dafont-arkhip-gf-lexend-giga: A c as open as a bent paperclip gives Arkhip its signature, with every letter floating well apart. Lexend Giga brings flat, single-weight linework and generous tracking, so paragraphs glide along with each word given room.
gen-dafont-arkhip-gf-lexend-mega: Lexend Mega reads like it was drawn with one nib. Arkhip is best at floating, geometric display letters, while Lexend Mega is best at a tall body height that nearly matches the capitals.
gen-dafont-arkhip-gf-lexend-peta: Lexend Peta reads wide-mouthed and approachable, its curves never thinning and its big x-height leaving little room for ascenders. Arkhip handles the floating, geometric display work; this body handles the text.
